purpose: Test strong knapsack inverse-degree statements against the binary near-half-variable dynamic PC obligation.

sources.authors: Michael A. Forbes, Amir Shpilka, Iddo Tzameret, Avi Wigderson
sources.title: Proof Complexity Lower Bounds from Algebraic Circuit Complexity
sources.read: Proposition 5.3 and the surrounding inverse-degree discussion; Appendix A Theorem A.4 and its characteristic-zero scope.
sources.use: Field-scope screening only; no general knapsack PC theorem imported into the claim registry.
sources.redistribution: PDF and extraction stay in private session scratch and are not committed.

sources.title: New Bounds for the Ideal Proof System in Positive Characteristic
sources.version: ICALP 2025, LIPIcs volume 334, article 22, official HTML
sources.read: Theorem 6, Theorem 8 and Remark 9, Lemmas 17 and 19 with the inverse-degree proof and intervening Claim 18; Section 2.2 construction viewed for context.
sources.use: The stated finite-subfield coefficient and outside-target hypotheses trigger the recorded Frobenius lemma. Source IPS lower bounds are not PC degree lower bounds.
sources.redistribution: Only this original audit is committed; downloaded source HTML remains private scratch.

search_scope: Bounded primary-source search for near-half PC constants, knapsack, random formulas and binomial/code mechanisms; not an exhaustive literature review. Search snippets, secondary mirrors and the project's own preprint were not used as independent theorem evidence.
outcome: The tested subfield-offset instances have small dynamic PC degree. No suitable near-half Boolean family was obtained.
numerical_checks: None; an application of an existing all-parameter Frobenius rule, with a complete specialized proof. No new proof rule, tree or computational encoding is introduced.
